newsitem.title: UK: Schroders says never saw Co-op documents.
newsitem.headline: Schroders says never saw Co-op documents.

text.p: British investment bank Schroders Plc on Wednesday moved to clarify its relationship with companies controlled by Andrew Regan who recently failed in a controversial takeover attempt of the Co-operative Wholesale Society.

Schroders said it was purely a portfolio investor in the firms, Lanica and Galileo, although three employees of Schroder Investment Management had invested around 11,000 pounds ($18,000) in Lanica before knowing about the formation of Galileo, the vehicle used by Regan to bid for CWS which used confidential documents leaked by a CWS employee, which Schroders says it never saw.

Galileo, an offshoot of 31-year-old Regan's Guernsey-based investment trust Lanica, is the subject of a High Court order preventing the use of confidential CWS documents leaked to Regan by now dismissed CWS manager Allan Green.
Costs were last week awarded against Galileo, Lanica, Regan, Green and David Lyons, Galileo's chief executive.

Sources said this element of Galileo's outstanding commitments would be reviewed by the liquidator. The process of going through a company's books and its assets can often take up to a year, they added.

Galileo was left stranded after the attempted 1.2 billion pound ($2 billion) takeover of the 153-year old mutually-owned supermarkets-to-funeral parlours group collapsed last week under CWS legal action and the withdrawal of financial backing.

"It was set up solely as a bidding vehicle," said one banking source, adding that it had assets of around 10 million pounds. Regan, Galileo's chairman, has not commented on the failed bid. He and Lyons face a private prosecution by the CWS.
Schroders Investment Management, Jupiter and stockbrokers Killik & Co were all shareholders in Galileo.

On Tuesday Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said it had started an investigation into a controversial 2.4 million pound payment to a third party in a deal between a company Regan ran at the time and the CWS in 1995. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
